video_title: Chris Paul: Why Soccer Still Isn’t Reaching the Hood + The NBA Lesson Mbappe & Vini Need

quotes.speaker: Chris Paul
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Paul on the difficulty of adjusting to life after basketball
quotes.excerpt: It's hard. I'm going through my process, and it's got its ups, got its downs.
quotes.quote: It's an understatement. Different is an understatement. It's hard. I'm going through my process, and it's got its ups, got its downs. There's a lot of benefit from being retired. I'm getting a chance to show up for my family and my kids, but I'm trying to get a new routine.

quotes.speaker: Chad 'Ochocinco' Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Ochocinco on the importance of maintaining discipline after retiring from sports
quotes.excerpt: You still have to train somewhat in some magnitude and stay active in a sense.
quotes.quote: Most of the time things change. I look at some of the people, whether it be NBA or NFL, once they stop playing, a lot of people can balloon a little bit. You have to watch what you eat. You still have to train somewhat in some magnitude and stay active in a sense. For some reason, I want to be one of those ones who doesn't play anymore and gets big. I stop moving, Chris, and I get small. I get skinny to a point where I look sick, and it makes me very uncomfortable.

quotes.speaker: Chris Paul
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Paul and Ochocinco discuss their competitive nature in one-on-one matchups
quotes.excerpt: I think I got him. Once I get in his head mentally, the game is mental before it's physical.

text_blocks.text: Leave that alone. Leave that alone.

text_blocks.speaker: Chad 'Ochocinco' Johnson

quotes.speaker: Chris Paul
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Paul on how his children's interest in soccer influenced his own
quotes.excerpt: His passion for it brought me into it even more.
quotes.quote: When I had kids, my son and my daughter played. Little Chris was so nice. My son actually played soccer and didn't play basketball for the two seasons that I played in Houston for the Rockets. He was left-footed. I took him to FC Barcelona, took him to practice, got to see Griezmann, got to see Pique, all of them. His passion for it brought me into it even more.

quotes.speaker: Chris Paul
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Paul defends the value of AAU basketball programs
quotes.excerpt: I'm not in the NBA without AAU basketball, that travel basketball.
quotes.quote: I got a very different opinion on this stuff. A lot of times people say this and that about AAU. My grassroots program, this is the 20th year I've had my AAU program. We got 14 kids that play in the NBA. It's just like with anything, some programs don't do everything right. There's a lot of really good AAU teams, and I'm not in the NBA without AAU basketball, that travel basketball. But you still got to have the discernment in making sure that you're not burning kids out.

quotes.speaker: Chris Paul
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Paul on his experience playing with Victor Wembanyama in Paris
quotes.excerpt: It was cool to see Vic just get excited because we were basically in his hood.
quotes.quote: I had a chance to play with Wembanyama last year, and we actually played in Paris in a preseason game. I remember we was leaving practice, and it was cool to see Vic just get excited because we were basically in his hood. We had practice at the place where he used to play at, and there's a perspective where I'm his teammate, but also got kids of my own. Vic pointed at these apartment complexes, and he was like, 'Yeah, that's where I lived at when I played for this team.'

quotes.speaker: Chris Paul
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Paul on the challenges of young players entering the NBA
quotes.excerpt: When Vic said that to me, all I could think about was what I'd been ready at that age.
quotes.quote: I'm not sure it's too young because you already can't go out of high school anymore. But it's tough. All these decisions that have to be made. When Vic said that to me, all I could think about was what I'd been ready at that age. And then I thought about it as a parent. I was like, man, hell no, my kid ain't. Because just some of the things that you think about growing up.

quotes.speaker: Chris Paul
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Paul's advice to young athletes about maintaining their childhood
quotes.excerpt: Remain a kid as long as you can, because when it becomes a job, it is a job.
quotes.quote: I say remain a kid as long as you can, because when it becomes a job, it is a job.

quotes.speaker: Chris Paul
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Paul on why he admires Cristiano Ronaldo's longevity
quotes.excerpt: As you get older, and you see people still playing at a high level.
quotes.quote: I'm going to tell you somebody who I've just always sort of admired and looked at, to tell you the truth, was Ronaldo. And I say that because as you get older, and you see people still playing at a high level and all the training and the workout that goes into it, because what, I'm 41, what he, 39 now, or 40? He's a year younger. I remember when I was 40, he's a year younger. And so, I don't care what anybody says, when you look at people that's around your age or what not, when Tom Brady was doing what he was doing, like for me to still be playing in the league, I'd be like, okay, boom, okay, good. That pushes you, drives you.

quotes.speaker: Chris Paul
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Paul on the importance of discipline and dress codes in the NBA
quotes.excerpt: If your jersey was untucked during practice, it was going to be a pink slip in your locker.
quotes.quote: When I first came in and I played for B-Scott, shout out to Byron Scott, man. Listen, if your jersey was untucked during practice, it was going to be a pink slip in your locker. They give you a warning one time, then it was a $100 fine. But that was just the discipline, the order, and all these things. Fast forward, I went and played for some different teams. When I got to Houston, Mike D'Antoni, it was almost a culture shock to me. You wear whatever you wanted to practice. I mean, whatever you wanted to practice, as long as there was some type of black and red in there. And that's where I was like, okay, just win games. Control what you can control. Just win games.

quotes.speaker: Chris Paul
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Paul on the importance of cross-sport support for athletes
quotes.excerpt: It's been really cool is NBA players showing up at their matches and them showing up at ours.
quotes.quote: What's been really cool is NBA players showing up at their matches and them showing up at ours. We took our whole team last year when we were in Paris, we went to go see PSG play. So, I think that type of connectivity, you start doing like cross-sports and getting a chance to integrate those cultures, I think you'll start getting both fans checking out both sports.

quotes.speaker: Chris Paul
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Paul on his brief trade to the Los Angeles Lakers
quotes.excerpt: I was traded there for a few hours.
quotes.quote: I was traded there for a few hours. My team at the time was owned by the league. Right. So the owner at the time had lost the team financially, and so the NBA owned the team. So when the trade went through, I guess all the other owners, because they sort of had ownership in the team, got a chance to have their say, 'Hell no.'

quotes.speaker: Chris Paul
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Paul on his reaction to the vetoed Lakers trade
quotes.excerpt: I've thought about it plenty of times, but I'm also a firm believer everything happens for a reason.
quotes.quote: I've thought about it plenty of times, but I'm also a firm believer everything happens for a reason.

quotes.speaker: Chris Paul
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Paul on the importance of basketball IQ and leadership
quotes.excerpt: Everybody think you can throw all these forwards on the court and just say go win the game.
quotes.quote: Everybody think you can throw all these forwards on the court and just say go win the game. No, that ain't happening. You still need some guys out there that know the playbook, that know how to orchestrate the game or what not. And if you come across a guy who ain't 6'2, you know, that's 6'6, 6'1 or what not, they going to be just fine.

quotes.speaker: Chris Paul
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Paul on the importance of role players in the NBA
quotes.excerpt: Role players are important. Very important, like people who know their role.
quotes.quote: Role players are important. Very important, like people who know their role. Like when you watch OKC play right now, guys got injured or what not, but everybody, they try to star in their role. Like they know Shai is the guy. Everybody knows that. When J-Dub is playing, he's the second guy. But when guys understand that, teams just find a way to rise.

quotes.speaker: Chris Paul
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Paul on the trend of teams prioritizing size over skill
quotes.excerpt: Everybody think that they going to be the next Wembanyama just because they tall.
quotes.quote: I think all sports tend to have these sort of trends. Everybody think that they going to be the next Wembanyama just because they tall, and everybody think that they going to be KD because they tall. But KD probably be the first person to tell you, and I don't know, but you still need some basketball IQ and some smarts.

quotes.speaker: Chris Paul
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Paul on the evolution of the point guard position
quotes.excerpt: It seems like those that are a little shorter aren't getting the same opportunities as they did before.
quotes.quote: It seems like those that are a little shorter aren't getting the same opportunities as they did before, because the game is evolved in a different direction.

quotes.speaker: Chris Paul
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Paul on the importance of open communication between coaches and players
quotes.excerpt: I think my relationships with coaches, more so being a point guard, is that everything was a conversation.
quotes.quote: I think my relationships with coaches, more so being a point guard, is that everything was a conversation. Everything ain't always going to be perfect, but I always wanted to have that dialogue with them. I feel like we got to, we got to be able to talk. If can't nobody else on the team talk, I got to be able to give you a pulse of the team. You're not in the locker room with us. So if I'm really an extension of you, I got to know how to, you're not being a snitch or what not, but when coach come in and he like, 'Yo, we just lost this game, we just lost our fourth game in five nights,' and coach like, 'We got practice tomorrow at 11.' That's where I'd be like, 'Hey coach, the guys might need a mental break.'

quotes.speaker: Chris Paul
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Paul on the need for a penalty for tanking in the NBA
quotes.excerpt: I think you're right about a penalty for it, and I think the competition committee continues to brainstorm.
quotes.quote: I think you're right about a penalty for it, and I think the competition committee continues to brainstorm stuff. But you don't have other teams to relegate. Where you going to go get a team from? You going to put one of the top AAU teams up there, and they going to be right back.

quotes.speaker: Chris Paul
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Paul on why he prefers his son to be a role player
quotes.excerpt: At his age now, my son just turned 17, and to see all the work he's putting into basketball.
quotes.quote: At his age now, my son just turned 17, and to see all the work he's putting into basketball now, I'd rather him be the sixth man. That's a hell of a question. But if you asked me that maybe seven years ago when I was at FC Barcelona and all that, I would absolutely say that.
